analysis.title: The Machines Are Coming For The Bond Shorts
key_insights: The US 10-year yield fell from about 5.30-5.35% (October 8) to roughly 4.9%, which is channel support. The 100-day moving average is slightly lower, around 4.8%.
The Market Ear's October 8 note flagged that everybody expected higher yields, and that crowding was the problem. The reversal followed.
JPM warned in early October that CTA momentum signals in Treasuries and Bunds were at extreme bearish levels, leaving trend followers heavily short and exposed to a sharp mean reversion.
The MOVE index is around 100 after easing. It averaged around 75 before the recent rates turmoil, so bond volatility is still elevated.
DB says CTAs have covered only a fraction of their bond shorts despite the Treasury rally, so the positioning unwind may not be finished.
GS expects CTAs to buy Treasuries this week: about $2.5mn DV01 each in the 2-year and 5-year, and $1.5mn DV01 each in the 10-year and 30-year.
GS says short-term CTA signals have flipped positive and medium-term signals are close to flipping. A further rally could trigger another wave of systematic buying.
The Market Ear frames the move as a CTA-driven flow story, not necessarily a fundamental bullish call on Treasuries.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield was at the top of its trend channel when positioning was crowded for higher yields.
The yield is at trend channel support after the decline. The 100-day moving average is around 4.8%.
Bond volatility is still elevated versus the pre-turmoil average of about 75, despite the recent retreat.

risk_factors: A further Treasury rally could trigger medium-term CTA trend signals and set off another wave of systematic buying.
CTAs still hold a large part of their bond shorts, so the unwind may continue.
Bond volatility (MOVE at 100) is still above its pre-turmoil level.
